en: The Apadāna of the Elder Lasuṇadāyaka Kuṇḍadhānavagga 7 I gave a garlic bulb to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher, the One with Vision. Because of that deed, I was reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. From there, having passed away, I was reborn here in the human world; there I was born into a wealthy family, possessing great splendor. In my final existence, I was reborn in the city of Sāvatthī; there I was known as Lasuṇadāyaka, a man of great wealth. I gave alms-food to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher, the One with Vision. Because of that deed, I was reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. “At that time, I was a forest-dweller not far from the Himālayas;
I lived off garlic.”
Garlic was my food.
Having filled cartloads of it,
I went to the monastery of the Saṅgha.
Joyful with a joyful heart,
I gave garlic to the Saṅgha of Vipassi,
the bull among men.
Devoted to the Teaching,
having given garlic to the Saṅgha,
I rejoice in heaven for an eon.
In the ninety-first aeon,
I was then Lasuṇa Yamada;
I do not recall ever being born in an unhappy state.
This is the fruit of garlic:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Lasuṇadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Lasuṇadāyaka.
